abstract: Fintech UX design is the user experience (UX) and user interface (UI) work behind software that moves, tracks or advises on money: account opening and identity checks, payments and payouts, portfolio and P&L dashboards, and AI assistants that answer money questions. ui-ux.agency, the design team of tkxel, designs fintech SaaS and AI products for US teams, with the rules that shape each screen (KYC, FINRA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, WCAG 2.2 AA) built into the flows from the first sketch.

challenges.headingOverride: Why is fintech UX design harder than other SaaS design?
challenges.answerNote: CardList on industry pages gets no `intro` prop (page.tsx line 97), so the H2 is followed by H3 cards, not by an answer paragraph. That breaks the layout rule 'h2-then-text'. Either the orchestrator passes an intro (one-line template change: intro={i.challengesIntro}) or the first card opens with the bold answer. cards.title: Identity checks sit in the sign-up flow
points: US banks must collect at least name, date of birth, address and an identification number before opening an account (FinCEN CIP rule, 31 CFR 1020.220). Fintechs and their partner banks run similar checks.
Document capture, selfie or liveness checks and manual review add waiting time a normal SaaS trial never has.
Design job: explain why each field is needed, save progress, show live verification status, give a clear path when a check fails.

cards.title: Trust has to exist before the first deposit
points: A user hands over a bank login or a Social Security number before seeing any value.
Design job: say who holds the money, show fees and transfer timing up front, write error messages that say what happens to the funds.

cards.title: Disclosures and marketing copy are regulated
points: FINRA Rule 2210 requires broker-dealer communications, including websites, apps and social posts, to be fair and balanced and to state material risks. It bans promissory claims.
Design job: place risk text where the decision is made, not in a footer link, and give compliance a screen-by-screen review file.

cards.title: Dense numbers on a phone screen
points: P&L, balances, positions and limits compete for the same space.
TradeZella's old interface hid the metrics traders care about under clutter (case study). Tie this to the case-study rail above.

cards.title: AI answers about money carry real risk
points: CFPB estimated that about 37% of the US population (98 million+) interacted with a bank chatbot in 2022. Its June 2023 issue spotlight warns about wrong answers, 'doom loops' with no way to reach a person, and privacy risks.
Design job: scope what the assistant answers, show the source, and offer a visible human handoff.

cards.title: Accessibility is a legal exposure, and so is login
points: DOJ's March 18, 2022 ADA guidance says businesses open to the public must make web content accessible and names WCAG as helpful guidance.

WCAG 2.2 (W3C Recommendation, October 5, 2023) adds SC 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (AA): no memory or puzzle test at login without an alternative such as paste and password-manager support. It also adds SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum): 24×24 CSS pixels.
Design job: one-time codes that can be pasted, passkey support (NIST SP 800-63-4, July 2025, covers syncable authenticators), and tap targets that pass 2.5.8.

challenges.cardLength: 30–55 words per card body. Each card names one rule or fact with its value and one design job. No card may list rule names without explaining them.

solutions.headingOverride: What does our fintech UX design work cover?
solutions.renderNote: page.tsx renders `solutions` only when the page has NO `sections` (line 110). Keep `sections` empty or the challenges, bullets and solutions blocks all disappear.

cards.title: KYC and account opening
points: Step order that asks for the easy fields first and the ID document last, a progress indicator, save-and-resume, camera guidance for document capture, and a clear 'we are reviewing' state with expected timing.
Designed around your identity verification vendor's SDK screens. We do not choose the vendor or set your risk rules.
Link: SaaS onboarding design (anchor = hub anchor).

cards.title: Payments, transfers and payouts
points: Fee and timing shown before confirm, a status tracker after send (pending, sent, arrived), and receipts users can find again.

Card entry: keep card fields inside the processor's hosted fields. PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirements 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 (mandatory since March 31, 2025) cover scripts on payment pages, so fewer third-party scripts on that page is a design decision as well as a security one.
Proof: the Anyday App redesign added real-time transfers and a balance that sits above recent activity (case study wording).

cards.title: Trading, portfolio and spending dashboards
points: One headline number per view, color plus sign or label for gain and loss (never color alone, WCAG 1.4.1), and drill-down from summary to transaction.
Proof: TradeZella net daily P&L, win-rate and profit-factor widgets and a dashboard each trader can arrange (case study wording). Link: TradeZella trading journal redesign.

cards.title: AI assistants and copilots for money questions
points: Answer cards that cite the account data or policy they used, a stated scope ('I can explain fees, I cannot give investment advice'), confidence and refusal states, and a one-tap handoff to a person.
Link: AI UX design agency. Do NOT also link chatbot-ui-design here: it already sits in the services grid.

cards.title: Compliance-aware flows
points: Consent screens for sharing bank data with third parties. Note: the CFPB personal financial data rights rule (Section 1033), finalized in October 2024, is under reconsideration (ANPR August 2025), so design consent to be clear and revocable, not to one rule text.
Disclosures placed at the decision point, dispute and error-report flows, audit-trail views for admins.

SOC 2: the AICPA Trust Services Criteria have 5 categories (security required; availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy optional). Design supports controls such as role-based access, session timeouts and activity logs. The auditor, not the designer, attests.

cards.title: Accessible fintech by default
points: WCAG 2.2 AA as the design target: contrast, focus order, 24×24 px targets, accessible authentication, and error messages that say how to fix the field.
If you also sell in the EU, the same flows have to meet GDPR consent and data-access rights. This is the only GDPR mention on the page.

cards.title: More people finish sign-up and verification
points: Fewer abandoned identity checks means more funded accounts. Give no generic % and no benchmark: none is sourced.

cards.title: Fewer 'where is my money' tickets
points: Status trackers and plain-language errors answer the question before it reaches support or the chatbot.

faqs.headingOverride: What do US product teams ask about fintech UX design?

items.q: Do you design KYC and identity verification flows?
items.aHint: Yes. Cover the step order, CIP fields, save-and-resume and failure paths, and design around the client's verification vendor SDK. Link SaaS onboarding design only if it is not already linked in the solutions card (one link per target per page).

items.q: Can UX design make our fintech product compliant with SEC, FINRA or PCI DSS rules?
items.aHint: No. Compliance is decided by your compliance team, counsel and auditors. Fintech UX design makes the required disclosures, consent and controls usable, and hands reviewers an annotated screen file. Mention the SEC's predictive data analytics proposal for broker-dealers and advisers, withdrawn June 12, 2025: there is no SEC rule on AI-driven 'nudges' in apps today, but FINRA Rule 2210 still governs communications.

items.q: How do you design AI assistants for financial products?
items.aHint: Scope, sources, refusal and low-confidence states, human handoff, CFPB 2023 spotlight risks (wrong answers, doom loops). Link the TradeZella or Anyday case study only if it is not used elsewhere. Neither case study includes an AI feature, so do not imply one did.

items.q: Which accessibility standard do you design fintech products to?
items.aHint: WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Mention DOJ ADA guidance from 2022, SC 3.3.8 and SC 2.5.8, and Section 508 when a product sells to federal agencies.

items.q: Have you designed fintech products before?
items.aHint: Yes. TradeZella: a SaaS trading journal and analytics product, redesigned for web and mobile: +40% user interaction, +25% retention, +30% new customers. Anyday App: a wallet and payout platform from XTM Inc. that lets hourly staff reach earned wages right away: 14 hours per week saved with automated payouts, +20% business clients. Use the case-study wording only. Do not call TradeZella a broker or regulated platform. Do not say we did KYC or compliance work on either.

items.q: How much does fintech UX design cost?
items.aHint: There is no separate fintech price, so do not invent a fintech premium. Use the published ranges: MVP design $15,000–$50,000, AI UX design $25,000–$90,000, SaaS product design $40,000–$180,000, a SaaS product redesign $50,000–$200,000 (service JSON priceRange). Link UI UX design cost. Note: home.ts says 'SaaS product design $40,000–$180,000' and the saas-product-redesign hub says $50,000–$200,000, and both are correct for their scope. Name each range with its service.

honesty.caseStudies: Only TradeZella and Anyday App tag industries: [fintech]. Quote only their files. TradeZella is a SaaS trading journal and analytics product (live data, charts, order execution, journal, analytics). Do not call it a broker, exchange or FINRA-regulated firm. notes: Write content/industries/fintech.json with: slug, title 'Fintech', order, anchor 'fintech UX design', centralEntity, sourceContext, metaTitle, metaDescription, keywords, hero, abstract, summary, intro, bullets, stats, challenges, solutions, benefits, process, faqs, relatedServices, headings, cta, semantic { entities, ngrams, skipgrams }, updated. No `sections`. useDefaults false (own benefits and process).

American English, USD, dates like 'October 5, 2023'. Expand on first use: user experience (UX), user interface (UI), know your customer (KYC), Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS), Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).
Banned words from RULES.md apply (seamless, leverage, cutting-edge, 'According to', hedges).
Rule status facts change. The fact-checker must confirm on publish day: CFPB 1033 status, the SEC withdrawal, PCI DSS version and the WCAG 2.2 current version date.
